summary: Maine's last light station, built 1909 on the St. Croix River below Calais, after a red lantern marked the Narrows from 1892. Tower owned by a historical society; the Coast Guard keeps the light.

structures.type: brick tower (conical per the nomination; cylindrical per the archive and LighthouseFriends)
structures.status: standing, owned by St. Croix Historical Society
standing, privately owned, closed to the public

access.note: Tower owned by the St. Croix Historical Society; the archive records the station as not open to the public. Keeper's house a private residence, closed.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (maintains the light); St. Croix Historical Society (tower); private owner (dwelling)

events.note: Fixed red beacon (red lantern) on the south side of the St. Croix, about 2 1/2 miles below Calais, reported in a September 1892 notice to mariners; LighthouseFriends dates it to 15 July 1892; by 1893 moved from a tree to a post
A 100-square-foot site purchased, surveyed and marked with copper bolts
Original fourth-order Fresnel lens installed, per the archive; LighthouseFriends places the lens in the new tower after 1909
Tower, keeper's dwelling, oil house and bell house built in 1909
Tower received its white daymark, previously red
Fixed red changed to green, per LighthouseFriends
Station electrified around 1931; bell tower added at the same time (LighthouseFriends)
Fresnel lens removed to the Maine Lighthouse Museum in Rockland
Station deeded to the Washington County Vocational Technical Institute
Added to the National Register as Whitlocks Mill Light Station on 21 January 1988
St. Croix Historical Society awarded ownership of the tower under the Maine Lights Program
Keeper's dwelling sold to a private owner
VLB-44 LED optic installed, solar powered
Original fog bell remounted on the bell tower by the St. Croix Historical Society

corrections.why: The 1892 date is the red lantern on a tree, not the brick tower. The nomination, LighthouseFriends and the archive all date the tower and complex to 1909.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1892 aid was a red lantern hung from a tree and later mounted on a post; the brick tower and keeper's house of 1909 replaced it. The record's tower date of 1892 conflates the two.

The nomination dates an earlier light on Dochet Island to 1856 and says it was destroyed; LighthouseFriends gives 1857 for a light on St. Croix Island. The sources do not say whether these are one island or two lights, so the record does not merge them. The story gives both dates as context only.

notes_for_editor: The record's characteristic 'Iso G 6s' is not confirmed by any source read here; LighthouseFriends calls the current light a flashing green, and the Coast Guard maintains it. Check the Coast Guard light list before publishing a characteristic. Tower shape: the nomination says conical, the archive and LighthouseFriends say cylindrical; the story says only 'brick tower'. Lens: the archive dates the original fourth-order Fresnel to 1906; LighthouseFriends describes it in the 1909 tower and the 1931 change to green; the sources do not reconcile. The 1912 dismissal of Aaron V. Tucker and the 1912 commendation of Frank N. Jellison are LighthouseFriends claims with no primary record in the local corpus (Board reports in the corpus end in 1901); both are marked unverified. LighthouseFriends' references include personal recollections of keepers' families (Cheney, Reilly) and a rumour about Colin Whitlock; these are left out. Jasper L. Cheney: the archive ends his stint in 1955; LighthouseFriends says he retired in 1957 for ill health; left as the archive gives it, with the other reading in the note. The Board volume 1893-1894 cites scan pages 338-339; printed pages (37? and 38?) are not confirmed, so the footnote gives scan pages only. The 1897 Board quotation has no page in the local index. The Bulletin index is cited at its page 14 for the Ingalls entry; the efficiency-flag page (29) is the index's own reference and was not checked in the issue. Newspapers: a Chronicling America search for Maine papers (1892-1915) found a Lighthouse Board notice to mariners in the Daily Kennebec Journal of 16 September 1892, p. 2, which dates the red beacon to that summer and gives its position; it is used. The OCR there reads 'Vacon' for 'beacon' and 'ha#' for 'has'; only the unambiguous words are quoted. The other seven search hits were not read in full; a scan of several for the station name returned no matches or incomplete output. Keepers on the archive roster are all shown as 'keeper' (sole keeper); the roster's 1959-1961 gap (1955 to 1959) is in the archive. The archive's record for Joseph W. Jellison has no start year for Tenants Harbor; the story says 'before 1920' only. Fact-check 2026-10-27: the nomination's Dochet Island light (1856, destroyed) and LighthouseFriends' St. Croix Island light (1857) are presented as two dates the sources do not reconcile; the earlier draft called them a different station, which the sources do not show, so the record and story now agree. The nomination's OCR reads 'turminal' for 'terminal' in the lumber-shipping sentence; the story uses 'terminal'. The 1894 Board appropriation line (Whitlocks Mill light-station, Maine 250.00) is read from the OCR line on scan p. 338; the page image was not viewed in this check. Unsettled: the 1897 Board page number (annualreportlig02statgoog has no page index for that line) and the 1892 notice's OCR ('Vacon' for 'beacon'), which the story does not quote.
